newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down in dull trading on Wednesday and traders said the weak performance of the domestic A share markets had weakened fund demand.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 10.60 percent from 13.01 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.36 million lots from 2.1 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the sharp losses on the A share markets in the past two days made institutions borrow little on the repo market, depressing the repo rates.
In addition, state banks have withdrawn from the repo market after the central bank banned them from trading on the market, making volume very thin.
Traders said they expected the rates to move at the current levels on Thursday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday mainly on renewed rumours that the central bank would cut bank interest rates shortly, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 122.60 yuan from 121.33 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 1.19 million lots from 1.1 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to continue to rise in the next few days, led by the 10-year bond, the market leader.
